neighbours.label: a predicate saying a person resists being moved or stopped (hard to convince, tough to crack, nothing could stop her), peaking on ' to' or ' could', as opposed to physical difficulty or plain description
fire: My grandfather is famously hard to persuade once he has picked a side.
The old sergeant was tough to break even under long questioning.
Once she set her mind on the summit, nothing could stop her from climbing.
Their lead negotiator is very difficult to sway when money is involved.
The witness proved tough to rattle during two days in court.
Once he starts talking about trains, nothing could stop him for an hour.
The union's president is notoriously hard to intimidate in public.
Our toddler is impossible to reason with when she is tired.
quiet: My grandfather is famously tall and has picked a side table.
The old sergeant was tired and asleep during the long march.
Once she set her bag on the summit, she started eating her lunch.
Their lead negotiator is very fond of tennis when money is involved.
The floor proved tough to clean during two days of rain.
Once he starts the engine of the train, it runs for an hour.
The union's building is notoriously hard to heat in winter.
Our toddler is very sleepy and warm when she is tired.

short: how hard a person is to move or stop (guess)
notes: Card: ' to' x11, ' can', ' easily', ' could', ' difficult'; output suppresses 'correctly'. Probes are uneven: tough to crack 0.49, hard to convince 0.45, Nothing could stop her 0.72, but Nothing could wake him 0.14, difficult to solve 0.08, hard to climb 0.07, easy to open 0.05. The strongest reading, 'you'd have to use a ruler to measure' 0.94, is not covered. A guess at the shared pattern; it may fail.
